scope: Three-way Native HaWoR, Stage-3-BIR, and Stage-3-BIR plus Adaptive VDA demo
summary: A reproducible compositor now presents all three methods on one fixed timeline and reports Adaptive VDA improvements against both Native HaWoR and Stage-3-BIR.
evidence: The H.264 output is 1920x1080, 30 FPS, 300 frames, and 10 seconds; a complete decode audit passes and the video SHA-256 is 47e0b4ace938328641f175214f854eff620137fdcdcb82c42ba864e71e488766.
Five sampled timeline positions were visually reviewed and show three synchronized RGB/skeleton panels plus aligned Native, Stage-3, and Adaptive right-hand world-root trajectories.
The embedded and public JSON metrics match the frozen Native HaWoR and final Adaptive VDA summaries with maximum absolute difference zero.
Against Native HaWoR, Adaptive VDA improves W-MPJPE 8.214%, WA-MPJPE 7.026%, RTE 8.836%, and Accel 9.144%; the additional gains over Stage-3-BIR are 4.220%, 3.639%, 6.888%, and 0.555%.
lessons: A three-way presentation is necessary to separate the contribution of Stage-3-BIR from the additional contribution of Adaptive VDA.
Compositing already-audited, frame-aligned panels avoids another dependency on raw RGB while preserving the exact frozen clip and metric provenance.
limitations: The video is a visualization of one pre-frozen ordinary development sequence and does not represent universal per-sequence improvement.
Trajectory panels and aggregate labels use GT for evaluation display; Adaptive candidate generation itself remains GT-free.
next_actions: Obtain user approval before committing or pushing the new three-way demo and documentation.
Repeat the frozen comparison on an independent challenge set before claiming broad generalization.
